newsitem.title: UK: Latin America prominent in sugar freight demand.
newsitem.headline: Latin America prominent in sugar freight demand.

text.p: Business on London's sugar freight market picked up at the end of the week with Latin American nations once again the focus of demand as origins, shipbrokers said on Friday.
Czarnikow Rionda fixed 9/10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to west Africa at a reported rate of around $30, they said.
Brazilian shippers SIMAB quickly fixed their order for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Recife to Lagos for mid-March but no rate has yet been reported.
Lorico fixed 13,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Syria for 15/25 March and Tate & Lyle was said to have covered its Barbados-London order for a further 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar.

Of the day's new business, E D & F Man quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to Chittagong for mid-March and Dreyfus for 25,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Baltic/Black Sea for 17/20 March.
Tate & Lyle also quoted for 12,800 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio/Recife to Lisbon for 18/25 March.
In other news, Lloyds Shipping Intelligence reported that a further attempt to refloat the Cyprus-flagged freighter Nika II was to be made on Friday.
The 15,251 dwt vessel ran aground at Veracruz anchorage, Mexico, last month and efforts to refloat the ship have so far been hampered by bad weather.
It sailed from Abidjan on January 23 and was inbound to Veracruz to load a cargo of bagged sugar for Algeria.
Egypt could end up delaying some of its recent raw sugar purchases until the second half of 1997 due to port congestion, London sugar sources said on Friday.
Egypt's state refiner, the Sugar and Integrated Industries Company, asked suppliers to delay some shipments by up to four months due to a shortage of storage space.

But three or four vessels carrying about 20,000 tonnes apiece, thought to be Cuban raws as part of a total 750,000 tonnes ordered for this year's delivery programme, were already on the way to Egypt, they said.
